questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer disengages from the tractor.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on a wet road and slide on the water layer. This can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Stopping at a green light is a sign of impaired driving. Watch for behaviors like this. Impaired drivers may have drunk alcohol, be very tired, be using drugs, or be ill.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the pedal does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic brakes by pumping the pedal three times, then holding it down firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another problem.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check for all of the following, except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: When inspecting tires, check for proper tread depth, wear, cracks, and air pressure. Make sure all tires are the same size. The brand of the tire does not matter.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and have been repaired, or if they have been marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, you can reduce the amount of braking needed by:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift to a lower gear. This helps control your vehicle without using the brakes too much. Heavy braking downhill can overheat the brakes and reduce stopping power.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery right after rain begins because:

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires are not made to drive in wet weather.
The water has not yet absorbed the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first begins, the water creates a slick layer by mixing with oil and grease on the road surface that has not yet been washed away.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking capacity.
Work in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work in addition to other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not change the braking power of the vehicle. ABS only activates when the wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: The heavier the vehicle:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes need to work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes need to work.
questions.explanation: A heavier vehicle needs stronger brakes to stop it.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, check the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal level in just a few seconds.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you must:
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, the engine must be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: The more alcohol in the body:

options.text: The quicker the liver will digest the alcohol.
The less effect the alcohol will have on the individual.
The longer it will take to remove the alcohol from the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to remove the alcohol from the body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. More alcohol means it takes longer to leave your system.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes are prone to getting out of adjustment. Check your brakes regularly. All brakes must work properly and be adjusted for safe driving.
